findings: The candidate is identifiable as a Chimney Swift: the primary specimen has the characteristic slender cigar-shaped body, dark gray-brown plumage, paler throat, large dark eye, short tail with stiff-looking tips, and long narrow folded wings extending beyond the tail.

The plate contains exactly one complete primary specimen. It has one head, one short bill, two folded wings, one tail, and a convincing clinging posture; the far-side leg is naturally occluded. The detached head and wing are clearly separated supplementary studies.
The primary specimen and detached head now show short, broad-based bills consistent with the species and the clearest attached side-profile reference.
The visible foot, toes, and leg are now small and short relative to the specimen and plausibly engage the vertical surface.
The detached wing study is now elongated, narrow, swept, and sharply pointed rather than broadly fan-shaped.

Every visible identification, measurement, habitat, behavior, and field-mark line is legible and agrees with the proposed profile. The common name, scientific name, and family are correctly written as Chimney Swift, Chaetura pelagica, and Apodidae.

The published length, weight, and Cornell wingspan values match the plate: 4.7–5.9 in (12–15 cm), 0.6–1.1 oz (17–30 g), and 10.6–11.8 in (27–30 cm). Audubon publishes a slightly broader wingspan range, but the proposed Cornell range remains directly supported and is not a profile conflict.

The ruler is internally consistent: 4.7 in (12 cm) is at the bottom, 5.9 in (15 cm) is at the top, values increase upward, and “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” prevents it from being mistaken for the printed specimen’s scale.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
